key: It is said that the senses are great; greater than the senses is the mind: greater than the mind is the Reason; but what is greater than the Reason, is He.
s: Having named desire as the foe that drives a man to sin, Krishna, near the chapter’s close, ranks the powers within; Śaṅkara (Advaita), on 3.42, reads the closing ‘He’ as the Self, the witness of reason, and Rāmānuja (Viśiṣṭādvaita), on 3.42, as desire, strongest and most overpowering of all.
src: Śaṅkara, Gītā Bhāṣya 3.42, tr. A. Mahadeva Sastri (1901); Rāmānuja, Gītā Bhāṣya 3.42, tr. A. Govindacharya (1898); both archive.org

evidence.words: He, the Self, the witness of reason, is superior to reason. … Supposing the senses and all, duddhi inclusive, were quiet and passive, desire or lust, which is craving, deeply rooted in the heart, and rajzas-born, will yet assert mastery … That which then is the most strong and overpowering, vis., kama … is denoted by the pronoun ‘sah.’
evidence.gloss: [Śaṅkara, on 3.42:] He who is behind all, the dweller in the body, the Self, the witness of reason, is superior to reason. … [Rāmānuja, on 3.42:] Even if the senses, mind and intellect (buddhi) were all quiet, desire, rooted in the heart and born of rajas, would still assert mastery; that strongest, most overpowering thing, desire (kāma), is what the pronoun ‘sah’ (he) denotes.
